entry.title: Patio guides and answers
entry.summary: Plain-language guides to patio bases, drainage, frost and stone choice.

entry.title: Nine-tenths of it is underground
entry.summary: The pavers you see are the last inch. Everything that decides whether the patio is still flat in ten years is underneath them and invisible when the job is done.

entry.title: Water always finds the low spot
entry.summary: A patio should shed water like a roof does: away from the house, off the surface and out. That comes from the slope built into it, not from sand added later.

entry.title: Why the freeze beats shallow work
entry.summary: Ground here freezes and thaws many times over a winter. Each cycle lifts the soil, and anything sitting too close to the surface comes up with it.

entry.title: Stone is a budget, not a style
entry.summary: Picking the look is the easy part. What moves the price is the material itself and how much cutting it needs.

entry.title: What a real estimate includes
entry.summary: A lump-sum price tells you nothing. The useful ones are itemized enough that you know what you're buying.

entry.title: Ask us anything
entry.summary: You don't need to know any of this to get a good patio. That's our job. But if you have a question about your own yard, the drainage around your house, or a number someone gave you, just ask.

entry.title: What a paver patio actually costs
entry.summary: Nobody likes a vague number, so here is how a patio price is actually built: size first, then what is under it, then how hard it is to get to.

entry.title: Pavers, concrete or stamped concrete
entry.summary: All three can make a flat outdoor floor. They behave very differently after a Massachusetts winter, and that is the part worth understanding before you pick.

entry.title: Patios through a New England winter
entry.summary: A patio built right survives winter on its own. The things you do at the edges of the season are what keep it looking new.

entry.title: How to spot a good crew from a bad one
entry.summary: You are not expected to know stone. You are allowed to watch how someone works, and that tells you almost everything.

entry.title: Walkways, steps and aprons
entry.summary: A walkway is a small patio you use every day. Because you use it every day, the details that fail are the ones you will notice first.

entry.title: Where does your yard drain?
entry.summary: Before anyone talks stone, walk your yard after a real rain. Where the water goes tells you more than any plan.
